claims.text: The three core artifacts are all this trip and nothing on them conflicts: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry TRP-00307; the trace first and last fixes are 18:01:17 and 18:31:17 and the trip_record's started_at and ended_at are 18:01:17 and 18:31:17, so no timestamp runs backwards and the rider discharges the initial burden in POL-RD-08(a) on a matching trip identifier and consistent pickup-side timestamps.

Measured on the field POL-RD-01 makes governing, the excess clears both limbs of the threshold. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 22.6 against an optimal_distance_km of 18.0, an excess of 4.6 km and 25.56%: greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km, so the threshold is met. trip_record.actual_distance_km shows the same 22.6 km but POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing that rounded convenience copy for the threshold test, so the rider does not rely on it. Full disclosure under POL-GEN-02(1): EV-GPS-00307 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE.

The trace is impaired for POLICY purposes and not merely in the schema pre-pass: it carries one gap of 240 seconds, from 18:16:17 to 18:20:17, sitting inside the KPE stretch this rider disputes, and 240 seconds is well over the 90 second limit in POL-RD-07(a). The rider states the impairment openly rather than presenting the trace as clean: EV-GPS-00307 is at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE, and on this trip the two tests coincide — schema-impaired and policy-impaired.

No independent corroboration of the excess exists anywhere in this bundle, so POL-RD-07(ii) bars establishing the deviation on the gps_trace alone: the chat log holds zero messages and therefore no driver admission, the fare_breakdown's erp_gantries list is empty with tolls_erp at 0.00 so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, the driver's counterparty statement denies the detour instead of admitting the route, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is the identical 22.6 km figure that POL-RD-01 itself calls a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement, not an independent derivation.

The consequence the policy prescribes is escalation, and escalation is the disposition that protects this rider. POL-RD-07(iii) says that where an impaired trace has no independent corroboration the claim is not sustained on the present record and the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof is a data failure and not a finding for the driver; POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave the present state standing, and the fare here is payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION would leave the 29.95 charge in place, whereas an escalated amount is held rather than collected.

Escalation is independently compelled by the confidence arithmetic. The only artifact carrying the measured excess is EV-GPS-00307, and under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence may not exceed the weight_multiplier of the artifact that carries the deciding fact, so it is capped at 0.39 — below the platform-wide 0.70 floor, which fires POL-RD-10(1). The bundle_integrity_score is context and not the cap, and because the second candidate carrier (trip_record.actual_distance_km) is a copy of the same measurement rather than an independent one, the maximum-of-two-carriers rule does not lift the cap.

The driver's explanation takes him nowhere. 'KPE straight down, no exit. GPS always drops in the tunnel' names no road or segment, cites no evidence ID and invokes no clause. The traffic advisory for this trip is absent from the bundle — EV-ADVIS-00307-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, and its absence is itself citable — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all: with no advisory covering the window there is nothing to compare against the optimal corridor, and the driver's assertion is an uncited excuse that POL-RD-08 discards. Under POL-RD-13 an assertion tested against an absent advisory neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route.

The disputed overrun is not an artefact of the outage, which is why the amount should be held rather than left collected. Under POL-RD-07(i) the whole distance across the impaired stretch is bounded, at most favourably to the driver, by the 3.01 km straight line between the bounding fixes, yet the total excess is 4.6 km; the excess therefore cannot be located wholly inside the gap, and at least 1.59 km of it falls on sampled track outside the outage. The rider is not asking the tribunal to guess what happened inside the tunnel — the rider's point is that the billed distance exceeds the optimal route by more than the tunnel can explain.

If the tribunal is nonetheless able to decide the merits rather than escalate, the refund is arithmetic and runs the rider's way. The trip is METERED so POL-RD-02 applies and POL-RD-11 does not; the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 24.82 against a charged_total of 29.95, a refund of 5.1300 rounded up to 5.15. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and is 17.13% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND and the 90% full-refund share in POL-RD-02 is not reached. No ERP or toll line exists (0.00), so nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

This rider is not the serial claimant POL-RD-08 guards against, so no additional corroboration burden attaches to the claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the four-or-more-claims with one-or-fewer-substantiated condition is not met on this record and that factor may not be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a), POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on it alone and requires one of four independent sources — and none exists here. The chat log for this trip holds 0 messages, so there is no driver admission and no rider instruction (EV-CHAT-00307). The set of erp_gantries actually charged is empty and off-optimal-route ERP is SGD 0.00 (EV-FARE-00307), so the pass-through record places the vehicle on no corridor other than the one billed. With the trace impaired and no independent corroboration available, POL-RD-07(iii) fixes the outcome: the claim is not sustained on the present record and the ruling is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because what has failed here is the data, not the driver. Escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03: it replaces the ruling, issues no monetary outcome, and leaves the SGD 29.95 charge held rather than refunding any part of it pending human review.

Escalation is independently mandatory under POL-RD-10(3): the gps_trace is impaired under limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 by a 240-second gap inside a 1,800-second active window, and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is anywhere in the pool. On that trigger the judge must not issue a final ruling at all. EV-GPS-00307 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE.

The asserted excess of 4.6 km is carried by a single artifact, EV-GPS-00307, at weight 0.39 (impairment disclosed: GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, LOW_COVERAGE), and the trip_record figure is a copy of that same measurement rather than an independent carrier of the fact. POL-GEN-02(2) therefore caps confidence in any ruling resting on that fact at 0.39, which is below the platform-wide 0.70 floor, and POL-RD-10(1) escalates the case automatically.

POL-RD-08(b) puts the initial burden on the rider to show an excess measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, this trace being impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). Neither route is open on this bundle: the trace is impaired at 0.39 on GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE, and all four named independent sources — a chat-log admission, a charged gantry set off the optimal corridor, a statement admitting the route, an independently derived distance — are absent. The rider's asserted 4.6 km excess is not made out on this record.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest, on a trace assumed unimpaired, POL-RD-06 gives the rider nothing: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the threshold of 3, and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 260 is 0, below the 0.05 ratio, so no pattern is established and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) nor a driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) may follow. The rider's theory — that the driver left the KPE and rejoined it — requires an off-corridor excursion, and no part of the trace shows one. Across 158 fixes the derived speed profile runs from 43.5 to 46.9 kph with no stationary or low-speed fix, and under POL-RD-07(i) the whole impaired stretch is read as the 3.01 km straight line between its bounding fixes, which is expressly the reading most favourable to the driver. EV-GPS-00307 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE.

No traffic advisory covers this corridor in this window: EV-ADVIS-00307-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight 0.0, and its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-03 would require an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the trace's arrival at that segment, and that comparison cannot be run on this bundle at all. Neither party, therefore, can establish from any independent record what happened across the 240-second gap, which is exactly the state of affairs POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) send to a human reviewer.

ruling.explanation:
This case cannot be decided on the record; it goes to a human reviewer. The governing reason is POL-RD-07. The GPS trace for trip TRP-00307 (EV-GPS-00307) contains a 240-second gap between consecutive fixes, from 18:16:17 to 18:20:17, and that gap sits inside the KPE stretch this dispute is about. 240 seconds is well over the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), so the trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely in the schema pre-pass. As POL-GEN-02(3) requires, the artifact is named: EV-GPS-00307 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE (coverage 86.7%).

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a), POL-RD-07(ii) says a deviation may NOT be established on the trace alone; it must be corroborated by an independent source. There is none. The in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00307) holds zero messages, so there is no driver admission. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00307) charges no ERP gantries and shows no off-optimal-corridor pass-through, so the pass-through record places the vehicle on no other corridor. The driver's statement denies the detour rather than admitting the route. And the trip_record distance (22.6 km) is the same measurement as the trace, which POL-RD-01 itself calls a rounded convenience copy of the trace figure and forbids citing for the threshold test, so it is not an independent derivation. With no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) make escalation mandatory, and the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02(2) independently puts the case below the 0.70 floor under POL-RD-10(1): the only carrier of the measured excess is the impaired trace at 0.39, and the trip_record figure is a copy of that same measurement rather than a second independent carrier, so the maximum-of-two-carriers rule does not lift the cap. bundle_integrity_score is context only and is not the cap. Escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03: the SGD 29.95 charge is held, neither collected nor refunded, and no amount moves to either party.

On the surviving claims. The rider is right that on the raw figures the excess is 4.6 km and 25.56%, clear of POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km tests, and right that rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 raise no added corroboration burden under POL-RD-08. But the governing distance comes from an impaired trace, so the threshold test cannot be run to establish the deviation while that trace stands uncorroborated: the limb is undecided over the impaired stretch and supports neither a refund nor a payment. The rider's asserted refund, had the trace been clean, would be SGD 5.15 (charged_total 29.95 less recomputed_fare 24.82 = 5.13, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 under POL-RD-02); that figure is not awarded.

The driver is right that his profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern - deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed trips in 90 days - so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise - and right that the sampled speeds (43.5 to 46.9 kph, with no stationary fix) show no off-corridor stop. Those points confirm only that nothing is proven either way; they do not convert an undecidable stretch into a finding for the driver.

The traffic advisory for this trip is absent: EV-ADVIS-00307-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. The driver's traffic assertion ('KPE straight down, no exit. GPS always drops in the tunnel') therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and POL-RD-13 confirms it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. POL-RD-13 expressly preserves POL-RD-10(3) where, as here, the trace itself is impaired and no independent corroboration exists, so the missing advisory does not change the disposition in either direction.

No driver compensation is due: the fare billed 22.6 km, the same as the trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall over 1.0 km under POL-RD-04. No referral is issued, because no clause on these facts produces one: there is no POL-RD-06 pattern and no POL-RD-09(4) phantom gantry or surcharge line.

What would resolve this for the reviewer: an ERP gantry record for the trip, a GPS export restoring the fixes across the 18:16-18:20 tunnel gap, or a platform-derived distance independent of this trace. Any one of those would let POL-RD-07(ii) run and the deviation be decided on its merits. The open question of what happened inside the tunnel belongs to the reviewer, not to a ruling made now.

It carries a single 240-second gap between consecutive fixes, from 18:16:17 to 18:20:17, inside the KPE tunnel stretch that is the subject of the dispute, with coverage of 86.7% across the 1,800-second active window. That is a policy-level impairment under POL-RD-07(a), not merely a schema flag, and the artifact is carried at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE.

I have checked each of the four independent sources it names and none is on this bundle. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00307) holds 0 messages, so there is no driver admission and no rider instruction. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00307) shows an empty erp_gantries set and SGD 0.00 of tolls, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The driver's own counterparty statement denies the detour rather than admitting the route. And trip_record.actual_distance_km (22.6 km) is, in POL-RD-01's own words, a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement, so it is not an independent derivation. Under POL-RD-07(iii) the claim is therefore not sustained on this record and the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because what has failed is the data and not the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory.

The confidence arithmetic points the same way. The measured excess is carried by EV-GPS-00307 alone at weight 0.39, and the trip_record figure is a copy of that same measurement rather than a second, independent carrier, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.39 — below the platform-wide 0.70 floor — which fires POL-RD-10(1) as well. No referral fires. POL-RD-06(c) needs an established repeat pattern and there is none; POL-RD-09(4) has no unmatched charge line to attach to, the ERP and toll total being 0.00.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. The reviewer needs an independent record from inside the 240-second gap: a GPS export from a second device, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement placing the vehicle on or off the optimal corridor, a call log, or a contemporaneous photograph with its capture time.
